Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 35, English)
Kshaya Kriya: How Your Energy , Health, and Fortune Get Siphoned Off — and How Hawan Actually Rebuilds You

Sour ce: a live Ashaeiynn sangat satsang (~53 minutes), covering the thr ee forms of "kshaya kriya" (draining/weakening occult practice), how to r ecognize and counter them, and a detailed explanation of what hawan actually r epairs versus what mantra shakti alone can fix.
1. Intr oducing "Kshaya Kriya" (Draining/W eakening Practice)

1. Bhaiya introduces a category of occult practice called "kshaya kriya" ("shiin kriya" in casual pronunciation) — practices whose entire purpose is to drain or weaken something specific fr om a targeted person , rather than to attack them outright. 2. Kshaya kriya has thr ee distinct forms , discussed in order: energy-draining, body-draining (health), and Maya-draining (prosperity , social standing, money , and power).
2. Energy-Draining Kshaya Kriya: Timing-Specific Depletion

1. A key marker of this first form: if a practitioner puts in a lot of effort toward a task and it still feels dispr oportionately exhausting, their energy has likely been specifically drained for that task. 2. This kind of drain is highly specific to particular important moments — a specific function, an important meeting, work/workspace matters where the practitioner has a genuine stake, or an activity from which they stand to gain something. Outside of those specific windows, a person af fected this way can otherwise stay up as late as midnight with no unusual ef fect. 3. This drain is never constant acr oss an entir e day — if someone felt drained all day , every day , that would itself be a signal that something more serious is happening; the localized nature (draining only around specific high-stakes moments) is the actual identifying pattern of this specific kriya.
3. Body-Draining Kshaya Kriya: Health-Related Depletion

1. The second form manifests through the body: a decline in health despite good behavior or lifestyle choices — for instance, someone who drinks alcohol, smokes, or eats poorly might appear to suf fer no consequence, while a comparatively disciplined, sattvic person mysteriously develops health problems instead. 2. Specific examples given: unexplained drops in hemoglobin, insulin deficiency , cholesterol buildup (which in turn further reduces insulin production and raises blood sugar) — occurring even in people who eat well, exercise, and stay active, defying the ordinary logic of cause and ef fect. 3. A pointed claim about diabetes specifically: Bhaiya challenges the assumption that eating sugar alone causes diabetes, noting that many diabetics report never having eaten excessively — implying an unseen factor (this kind of kriya) can be at play alongside ordinary physical causes. 4. A statistic offer ed: roughly 85% of people under going standard medical treatment for such unexplained health issues do not fully recover and remain on ongoing treatment, while the remaining ~25% (whose issues are purely physical in origin) recover
in a week or two through diet and rest alone — this gap is of fered as one practical indicator that something beyond ordinary physical causes may be involved.
4. Maya-Draining Kshaya Kriya: The Siphoning of Fortune and Pr osperity

1. The third and most heavily used form of kshaya kriya operates on Maya — prosperity , social standing, money , and power . The cor e claim: what was destined to come to you (per your own kundli/fate) can be r edirected to someone else instead , without your knowledge. 2. The "government ration" analogy: just as government contractors and of ficials sometimes siphon of f only a fraction of allocated grain to the poor and split the rest amongst themselves, someone's destined fortune ("raj yog" or similar) can similarly be inter cepted and diverted befor e it ever reaches them , leaving the person with far less than astrologers repeatedly promise is coming. 3. Practical implication: if multiple astrologers or saints have told you that your kundli shows genuine wealth/potential ("raj yog") but you see none of it materializing, this teaching's advice is to check whether that fortune has simply been diverted elsewhere, rather than assuming the prediction was simply wrong. 4. Who typically engages in this form of theft: people who understand early on that their own destiny holds little for them, and who therefore learn to "cut the pipe" of someone else's incoming fortune instead — described using the phrase "koi doosre ki pipe kaatna" (cutting someone else's pipe).
5. Why the Education System Leaves People Vulnerable to This

1. Bhaiya criticizes the standard education system as preparing people only to become employees ("naukar") — teaching rules, regulations, and workplace etiquette, but never teaching people how to actually recognize or defend against unseen astral-world interference with their own destiny . 2. His pointed r emark: "struggle" as commonly discussed in career/education contexts (grinding through hard work) is compared to a horse's labor — implying that ordinary hard work alone, without understanding the astral dimension, isn't the missing ingredient for many people's stalled progress.
6. Vashikaran and Stambhan: Two Related, Better -Known Practices

1. Vashikaran vidya is described as control over another person's attention/obedience — someone (a parent, sibling, partner , or relative) becomes unusually influenced by or obedient toward a specific person, listening to them far more than seems natural. 2. Stambhan vidya is described as the deliberate severing or freezing of a close relationship — two people who were once inseparably close ("jigri," dearer than life) becoming unable to even look at each other , driven by jealousy from others who specifically wanted to break their bond (e.g., business partners or family members who benefit from their separation). 3. Kshaya vidya, by contrast, is comparatively obscur e — known mostly to tantriks themselves and referred to by many dif ferent regional names, but the underlying concept remains the same: something that should rightfully flow to you (ener gy , health, or fortune) is instead being diverted elsewhere.
7. Recognizing and Responding to Kshaya Kriya: The Monkey Analogy

1. A key behavioral principle: like monkeys, negativity generally leaves you alone until you make dir ect "eye contact" with it (i.e., become aware of and name it) — once you recognize and understand what's happening to you, the responsible negativity may escalate, since it now senses it's been identified. 2. Practical guidance: a person who genuinely wants to progress on their own must learn to observe and recognize negativity affecting them, rather than avoiding the topic — this recognition is itself "half the battle won," since awareness allows a person to put up active defenses instead of unknowingly absorbing repeated attacks. 3. Bhaiya's estimate: roughly 80-85% of people who come to Ashaeiynn arrive already significantly af flicted by negativity of this kind, often specifically given "a chance" because of some past good deed or service (seva) they performed, even if they don't consciously remember it.
8. "Shastra and Shastra" — Active Defense, Not Passive Endurance

1. Bhaiya explicitly rejects a purely passive, "Gandhian" (non-confrontational) approach to negativity: practitioners should hold both scriptur e (shastra/knowledge) and weapon (shastra/active mantra-based counter -action) — those who understand through knowledge should use it; otherwise, decisive counter -action ("mar do, phod do") is appr opriate. 2. Devotees of Ram ar e described as compassionate, not passively begging or weak — actively striking back (via mantra shakti in the astral realm) against a negativity or tantric attacker , rather than tolerating repeated harm, is framed as consistent with genuine devotion, not opposed to it. 3. A recommended pr ocess once an attacker is identified: counter -attack proportionally (e.g., if struck once, respond with a stronger counter) — and think carefully before attacking anyone unfairly in the first place, since this cuts both ways.
9. Ashaeiynn's Ongoing, Automatic Pr otection Layer

1. Cutting active tantric kriyas targeting a member is described as something Ashaeiynn's own shakti performs automatically for practitioners who attend hawan r egularly — members do not need to separately ask how to "cut" an attack; this happens on their behalf as part of consistent hawan attendance. 2. This creates an ongoing back-and-forth ("kashmakash") : the attacking tantrik/negativity will likely try again after being cut once (since ego/reputation is at stake for them too — "I've never been beaten before, and this newcomer just beat me"), so the practitioner should expect repeated cycles of attack and defense rather than a single, final resolution. 3. The practitioner's actual job during this ongoing cycle is simply to keep building their own jap shakti consistently — the defensive/counter -attacking work is handled by Ashaeiynn's shakti; giving up jap out of frustration or fear ("main dṛishti kholne kyun aaya," "main kahin aur chala jaata hoon") is explicitly discouraged, since abandoning practice halfway leaves a person exposed without having actually built anything durable.
10. Given vs. Earned Shakti

1. A key distinction: "di hui shakti le li jaati hai; kamai hui shakti aakhir tak chalti hai" (given shakti can be taken away; earned shakti lasts until the end). Bhaiya notes he could technically grant someone drishti quickly , but such a gift could just as easily be revoked later — whereas shakti earned through one's own sustained sadhna is durable and not contingent on anyone else's whim.
1 1. Practical First-Aid: The Three-Day , Eleven-Diya Cycle

1. When a practitioner notices they've been specifically drained/attacked (per the patterns above), an immediate first step is offering 1 1 diyas (lamps) to Hanuman Ji Maharaj — described as producing an immediate, "hand-to-hand" ener getic response. 2. This should be r epeated as a fixed thr ee-day cycle , even if relief is felt on day one — completing the full three-day cycle is recommended rather than stopping early , since an incomplete cycle risks the ef fect reverting. 3. Time and location of lighting the diyas ar e flexible — the specific ritual mechanics matter less than consistently completing the three-day cycle.
12. A Second-Stage Pattern: Family and Acquaintances Skimming Potential Fr om a Young Age

1. As a person's latent potential/siddhi becomes noticeable (sometimes even from childhood), relatives (aunts, uncles by various family terms) or acquaintances who can per ceive this potential may begin subtly skimming fr om it early on , often without the af fected person's awareness — of fered as an explanation for patterns like unexplained hair loss, declining social/romantic interest over time, or other gradual, hard-to-pin-down personal declines. 2. The broader point: anyone with any developed per ceptive ability (not just those following Ram-focused sadhna) can potentially "see" and act on a person's underlying situation — this is described as common and not exclusive to any single

tradition, which is also why cheaper , preta-based practitioners (char ging comparatively small sums) can also produce visible, marketable results, in contrast to the substantially more ef fortful discipline required to accomplish genuine Ram-mantra siddhi.
13. A Live Q&A: Can Kshaya Kriya Happen During the Day , Not Just at Night?

1. In response to a member's question, Bhaiya confirms kshaya kriya is not r estricted to nighttime — it can be performed at any time of day , and the person responsible could plausibly be anyone nearby , reinforcing that personal protection/awareness is each practitioner's own responsibility rather than something to assume away .
14. A Live Q&A: Is "W itchcraft" the Same as Tantric Practice?

1. Responding to a member's question comparing modern "witchcraft" practices to traditional tantrik kriyas, Bhaiya confirms: the underlying concept is identical r egardless of r egional name or practitioner gender ("tantrik mein ladka bhi aa sakta hai, ladki bhi aa sakti hai; witchcraft yeh sab same") — these practices exist worldwide, and a new regional or cultural label doesn't change the fundamental underlying concept.
15. A Live Q&A: What If My Family Doesn't Shar e My Devotion?

1. A member raised a thoughtful concern: if everything is surrendered fully to Hanuman Ji Maharaj, does the practitioner personally retain nothing of their own (comparing it to keeping valuables in a bank locker)? 2. Bhaiya's answer acknowledges the practitioner's own high level of surr ender and understanding, but adds a crucial caveat: family members (spouse, children, parents) may not share the same depth of devotion or understanding — a practitioner's own child, for instance, might not of fer the same heartfelt reverence to Hanuman Ji Maharaj that the practitioner themselves has cultivated through struggle and practice. 3. This is precisely why learning these pr otective "vidyas" for oneself r emains essential even for a fully surr endered devotee — because family members who haven't personally undertaken the same sadhna won't share the same protective shakti, and the practitioner needs to be equipped to protect the household as a whole.
16. Do Tantriks Face Karmic Consequences for Their Actions?

1. Asked whether tantriks who perform harmful kriyas ever face karmic consequences ("karm phal"), Bhaiya af firms: "jaise ko taisa hamesha hota hai" (like is always met with like) — karmic consequence is inevitable, though its timing and form aren't always immediately visible (illustrated with a light aside about hair loss as one small, mundane example of accumulating consequence).
17. What Hawan Actually Repairs vs. What Mantra Shakti Alone Can Fix

1. A crucial distinction: mantra shakti can r ecover what was lost specifically in the astral world, but r ecovering what was lost in the physical world r equires hawan specifically . If a negative kriya's ef fect is caught and cut immediately at the astral level, it can be neutralized "hands-on" via mantra shakti alone before it manifests physically . 2. However , once astral-level damage has alr eady pr ogr essed into a physical-world effect (e.g., ongoing stomach trouble caused by an earlier , uncaught kriya), simply cutting the original kriya at this later stage will not automatically heal the physical symptom — the underlying physical damage (described metaphorically as lost "agni"/ener gy within the af fected or gan) needs to be actively rebuilt, either through very substantial personal mantra shakti or through hawan's physical-world effect. 3. Analogy: if a physical structure like a house sustains damage, simply removing the cause of damage doesn't repair the structure itself — repainting, re-plastering, and rebuilding are still separately required. Hawan functions the same way for physicalworld damage caused by negativity — it is described as a necessary ongoing "supplement," ideally continued for life, rather than a one-time fix.

4. Bhaiya states this rule applies to him as well — hawan cannot change a person's fundamental "naseeb" (destiny/fortune); it specifically addresses physical-world damage caused by negativity , not a person's broader destined outcomes. 5. A clarifying summary of hawan's actual r ole: hawan alone builds shakti — it does not, by itself, make a person divine ("bhagwan"). What makes a person "bhagwan swaroop" (God-like in nature) is God's name (naam) working on one's own character , not hawan by itself. 6. The complete formula offer ed: hawan builds shakti; that shakti, combined with guru naam and guru parampara (lineage), gets properly and beneficially used; if genuine character (charitra) is added into this combination as well, a person becomes truly God-like in nature; and when all of these — hawan, naam, guru parampara, and character — come together , Bhagwan Narayan himself is said to manifest.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

Kshaya kriya (draining/weakening occult practice) comes in three forms: ener gy-draining (localized to specific important moments, not constant all day), body-draining (unexplained health decline despite good habits, or good health despite poor habits), and Maya-draining (fortune/prosperity diverted to someone else, like a government contractor skimming rations meant for the poor). If astrologers repeatedly promise wealth/potential ("raj yog") that never materializes, this teaching's advice is to check whether that destined fortune has been diverted elsewhere rather than assuming the prediction was simply wrong. Vashikaran (control over someone's attention/obedience) and stambhan (deliberate severing of a close relationship) are better - known cousins of the more obscure kshaya vidya, but all rely on the same underlying redirection-of-what's-rightfully-yours concept. Negativity behaves like a monkey — it tends to leave you alone until you make "eye contact" (recognize and name it); recognition is "half the battle won" since it lets you defend yourself instead of unknowingly absorbing repeated attacks. Hold both "shastra and shastra" (scripture/knowledge and active counter -action) — devotion doesn't require passive endurance of repeated harm; active mantra-based counter -defense is appropriate and consistent with genuine devotion. Ashaeiynn's shakti automatically cuts active tantric kriyas for regular hawan attendees — practitioners don't need to separately request this, but should expect an ongoing back-and-forth cycle of attack and defense rather than one final resolution, and should keep building their own jap shakti throughout. Given shakti can be taken away; earned shakti (through your own sustained sadhna) lasts until the end. First-aid for a noticed attack: of fer 1 1 diyas to Hanuman Ji Maharaj, repeated as a fixed three-day cycle (even if relief comes on day one, complete all three days). As latent potential becomes visible (sometimes from childhood), relatives or acquaintances with any developed perceptive ability may subtly skim from it — of fering a possible explanation for patterns like unexplained hair loss or declining social/romantic interest over time. Kshaya kriya isn't restricted to nighttime, and "witchcraft" is described as conceptually identical to traditional tantrik practice, just under a dif ferent regional/cultural name. Even a fully surrendered devotee still needs to learn protective vidyas personally , since family members who haven't undertaken the same sadhna won't share the same protective shakti. Tantriks who perform harmful kriyas do face karmic consequence ("jaisa karoge waisa bhrogoge"), though the timing and form of that consequence aren't always immediately visible. Mantra shakti alone can recover what was lost in the astral world if caught immediately; recovering physical-world damage already done requires hawan specifically — hawan functions as an ongoing "supplement," not a one-time fix, and this rule applies to everyone, including Bhaiya himself. Hawan alone builds shakti — it does not by itself make a person divine. God's name (naam) working on one's own character is what makes a person truly God-like; when hawan, naam, guru parampara, and genuine character all come together , Bhagwan Narayan himself is said to manifest. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .

Bot Response Guidelines (Session 35 additions)

When discussing kshaya kriya's three forms (ener gy , body/health, Maya), keep each form's identifying pattern precise — ener gy-draining is localized to specific high-stakes moments (not constant all-day fatigue), body-draining is health decline defying ordinary cause-and-ef fect, and Maya-draining is fortune/prosperity diverted elsewhere. Do not blur these into one another . When a user describes unexplained health issues (diabetes, hemoglobin, cholesterol) in relation to this teaching, present the "hidden factor" framing as this teaching's own explanatory claim, not as an independently verified medical fact — never contradict or replace actual medical guidance. When discussing "raj yog" or destined wealth that hasn't materialized, present the "diversion" explanation as this teaching's own perspective, not as an endorsement of blaming specific individuals without evidence. Keep the "shastra and shastra" (active defense) framing intact — this teaching explicitly rejects purely passive endurance of harm, but frames counter -action as mantra-based/astral, not real-world confrontation or vigilantism.

When discussing Ashaeiynn's automatic protection for hawan attendees, be clear that this is described as an ongoing back-andforth process, not a single guaranteed permanent fix — practitioners should expect to keep building their own jap shakti. Keep the given-vs-earned shakti distinction intact when answering questions about quick spiritual shortcuts — earned shakti through sustained sadhna is presented as more durable than anything granted. The 1 1-diya, three-day first-aid protocol should always be presented as a complete three-day cycle, not a one-time action, and never as a substitute for medical care in health-related contexts. Preserve the explicit distinction between what mantra shakti alone can repair (astral-level, caught immediately) and what specifically requires hawan (already-manifested physical-world damage) — never conflate the two roles. Preserve the closing formula precisely: hawan builds shakti; naam plus one's own character makes a person God-like; hawan + naam + guru parampara + character together is what is said to manifest Bhagwan Narayan. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .

Bhaiya's Teachings — Curated Conversational Supplement (Session 35, Hinglish)
Kshaya Kriya par Sangat ki Live Q&A
